plan.analysis: L1 is stuck at 0.940795: the resolution sweep to 2x N changed nothing, so finer grids alone are not the bottleneck. Two structural limits are visible in p0002's code: the log-parametrised L-BFGS freezes the support (active set = h > 1e-13*max), so the 20.9% zeros can never open and small entries can never vanish; and ||f*f||_inf is handled through a single argmax knot, which forbids flattening the peak plateau (42.8% of knots are within 5% of max). I bet on (1) active-set support moves using the gradient at zero entries, (2) a smoothed soft-max surrogate with temperature annealing so several near-max knots are driven down together, and (3) an independent coarse multi-start from random shapes, prolongated only if better, as a different basin rather than more polishing of the same one.

experiments.hypothesis: The support pattern has never been re-optimised: _lbfgs_log freezes active = h > 1e-13*max, so 20.9% forced zeros are permanent and near-zero spikes cannot die. Making the support a free variable (drop weak entries, admit entries whose gradient at zero is downhill) lets the optimiser reshape the tails, where the R deficit lives.
experiments.change: Add a working-set loop around _lbfgs_log. (a) Compute the full gradient g = _backprop(gLf, h) + 2/s for the current h including at zero entries, i.e. evaluate the gradient of val = -log(num)+2log(s)+log(max) at h with zero positions still zero (do not restrict to the active set). (b) Drop: set to exactly 0 the smallest 1% of positive entries whose removal does not increase val (or simply the 1% smallest h). (c) Admit: among zero positions, pick the 1% with the most negative g_i and set them to 1e-3 * mean(h). (d) Re-run _lbfgs_log with the new active set, keep the result only if R improves. Repeat this add/drop cycle inside the main loop until deadline-1.0 s, then run the existing peak/phase polish on the best. Report 'support: k zeros, R=...' after each cycle.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.9420 on L1 (from 0.940795). Success shows as a decreasing zero-fraction with better R in the support lines; if the zero count returns to ~21% each cycle, the support is already optimal and the plateau is elsewhere.

experiments.hypothesis: ||f*f||_inf is non-smooth; using only argmax(Lf) means the peak is pinned at one knot and nearby knots just under the max are unpenalised. A temperature-annealed soft-max penalises a whole plateau of knots, letting the peak region flatten and raising ||f*f||_2^2 relative to the max.
experiments.change: Add a second optimiser path using the surrogate val_tau = -log(num) + 2 log(s) + tau * logsumexp(Lf / tau), with gradient gLf = -dq/num + softmax(Lf/tau) (derivative of tau*logsumexp), backpropagated as now. Do continuation over tau = 0.02, 0.005, 0.001, 2e-4, 1e-4 times max(Lf), each stage an L-BFGS-B call on log-heights (reuse _lbfgs_log but with this value/gradient), maxiter 300 per stage. After the final stage run 200 more (exact) iterations with the current hard-max objective and take the result only if R beats best. Run this once from the start; if it improves, repeat the anneal from the improved point while time remains.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.9415. The diagnostic is the fraction of knots within 0.1%/1% of max (currently 19.5%/33.9%): success should raise the 0.1% fraction while ||f*f||_inf falls slightly for fixed ||f*f||_2^2; no change means the peak is already a single sharp knot that grading cannot smooth.

experiments.hypothesis: Every experiment so far has polished the same basin; the resolution sweep failing to move anything suggests a local optimum that improvements-of-the-same-kind cannot escape. Independent random shapes at coarse N, optimised and prolongated, probe different basins.
experiments.change: Before any polishing, allocate roughly the first 60% of the budget to a coarse multi-start: N_c = 512. Draw 10 random starts: heights = product of a random envelope (e.g. exp of a random walk with 3-6 random knot amplitudes interpolated over [0,N_c]) times a random sparse mask (each entry zero with probability drawn uniformly in {0.1,0.3,0.5}); ensure sum > 0. Run _lbfgs_log (the full-vector log-height version) with maxiter 400 on each within a per-start time slice; keep the best R_c. Prolongate the best to N = 16384, re-run _lbfgs_log 400 iters; then prolongate to the start resolution 84992 and polish with the existing _window_polish_peak schedule. Return whichever of this and the polished start has higher R.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.942. If none of the 10 coarse starts beats 0.940 after prolongation, that is informative: the shape class is genuinely narrow and future gains must come from support/peak smoothing, not from restarts. Report each coarse start's R so the shape diversity is visible.

plan.analysis: L1 is stuck at 0.940795. Every height-only polish, support working-set, softmax, random multistart, and smoothing experiment returned the start unchanged, so the frozen discrete support and relative placement of spikes are the likely bottleneck. F5 shows multiscale refinement works from a trivial start but is far below this basin. I am betting on changing support combinatorics directly: move/split/merge spikes, displace or rescale one cluster relative to another, and seed new support with a deterministic periodic modulation. Target is a measurable gain above 0.9408; unchanged results would confirm the current support is locally optimal.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002's heights are locally optimal but its nonzero support positions are frozen; F1 only added/removed zero entries by gradient, never moved existing spikes. Translating, splitting, or merging spike components should change the convolution overlap pattern and can escape the height-only local optimum.
experiments.change: Implement a support-move loop. From best, find connected nonzero components (threshold 1e-6*max) and local maxima. Repeat until deadline-2s: copy best; pick one component weighted by mass and either (a) translate it by an integer d in {-16,...,-1,1,...,16}, adding heights where it overlaps and clipping at array ends, (b) split it into two copies separated by d with half mass each, or (c) merge it with the nearest other component. Then run _lbfgs_log on all entries in a window spanning old and new positions plus 10% margin, followed by full _lbfgs_log. Accept only if R_of improves by >1e-9. Keep the best; print each accepted trial.
experiments.prediction: Aims for >=0.9410 on L1. A gain of >=1e-4 shows support combinatorics was limiting; no gain means the current spike positions are locally optimal and a full combinatorial reconstruction is needed.

experiments.hypothesis: The f*f maximum at 0.296 of support suggests the peak is set by the relative distance between two dense clusters. Whole-array phase shifts failed, but moving or stretching one cluster relative to the other changes the convolution plateau directly.
experiments.change: Split best at its largest zero gap (or at 0.5 if no gap). For delta in a schedule ±1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128 steps: copy best, shift the right part by delta (pad zeros, truncate if needed), then reoptimize all positive entries with _lbfgs_log and apply _window_polish_peak. Also try resampling the right part by stretch factors 0.98,0.99,1.01,1.02 using cumulative interpolation, then reoptimize. Accept the best; use remaining time alternating full and peak-window polish.
experiments.prediction: Aims for >=0.9410 on L1. A gain identifies the optimal inter-cluster spacing; unchanged means relative cluster placement is already locally optimal.

info.open_why: p0002 is the line's best and p0005 shows the only real gain path (multi-scale from trivial start), so I want their full code/results and F5's evidence to design experiments that either re-derive the good basin at higher N or exploit the 0.82 construction's structure.

plan.analysis: L1 is pinned at 0.940795: every local perturbation, support move, smoothing, phase shift and soft-max objective returned p0002 unchanged. The strongest untested lever is that p0002's resolution sweep was hard-truncated at 2x its starting N, so it stopped at 84992 without ever running at 130k+. I am betting on (i) a true resolution ladder beyond 2x, (ii) a symmetry-changing construction (mirror completion), which is a different basin because the ideal flat f*f is symmetric, and (iii) a direct flat-target objective that fits a rectangle of the same L1 instead of locally differentiating the ratio. These are larger changes than the failed perturbations and each tests a distinct structural assumption.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002's sweep only reached 2x its initial N (84992); finer steps may resolve narrower features and raise R, as the 42496->84992 step did.
experiments.change: Replace the fixed (N,1.5N,2N) sweep with an unbounded ladder from start: Nt in [130000,200000,300000,450000,650000,900000,1000000], stopping at deadline-5s. For each Nt: hp=_prolongate(best,Nt); hp=_rescale(hp); run _lbfgs_log(hp,300,deadline), then _window_polish_peak(hp,deadline,0.35,32), then another _lbfgs_log(hp,200,deadline). Keep best if R improves, but carry best forward even when a level does not improve. Print R at every Nt; use FFT convolution and leave 2s margin.
experiments.prediction: Target >0.9410 (ideally 0.9415). If R rises monotonically with N beyond 84992, resolution was limiting; if it stays 0.940795 at all N, the continuous basin is converged.

experiments.hypothesis: p0002 is asymmetric with the f*f peak at 0.296; the ideal flat f*f is symmetric, so mirror-completing f may enter a different, possibly better basin that local asymmetric perturbations cannot reach.
experiments.change: From start, form h0 = start + start[::-1] (N doubles to 169984), _rescale, and run the existing multi-scale pipeline: _lbfgs_log(h0,400,deadline); then _window_polish_peak at frac 0.10,0.20,0.35,0.50,0.75 with full _lbfgs_log after each; then repeat full+peak polish until deadline-2s. Also evaluate h0 before optimization and print its R. Keep the mirror-completed result even if it initially scores lower, and compare final R to 0.940795.
experiments.prediction: Target >0.9420. A gain means the asymmetric p0002 was a local trap and a symmetric basin exists; a large drop means symmetry is structurally worse for this ratio.

experiments.hypothesis: The ratio gradient only constrains argmax and L2, so it cannot easily fill valleys of f*f. Fitting an explicit flat rectangle with the same L1 targets the true equality case of Hoelder and may move off the p0002 plateau.
experiments.change: Coarse-grain start to Nc=4096. Compute L0=_knots(hc), M=max(L0), S0=sum(L0). Let plateau=[j: L0_j>=0.10*M], a=min(plateau), b=max(plateau), w=max(1,int(0.05*(b-a))). Build normalized shape q=1 on [a+w,b-w], linear ramps of width w to 0 at a and b, 0 elsewhere; set T=(S0/sum(q))*q. Minimize F(h)=sum_j (L_j-T_j)^2 + lambda*(sum(h)-sqrt(S0))^2 with h>=0 on the Nc grid via L-BFGS-B (additive bounds 0..inf), lambda=10*(M/sqrt(S0))^2, using the existing _backprop for the convolution adjoint. Run up to 500 iterations, _rescale, then prolongate 4096->8192->32768->84992, running _lbfgs_log and _window_polish_peak at each level; keep the best R. Print the final flatness residual sum(L-T)^2 and R.
experiments.prediction: Target >0.9415. If R rises while residual falls, direct flat-target fitting found a better basin; if residual falls but R does not, the rectangle is unattainable and the ratio plateau is intrinsic.

info.open_why: p0002 is the incumbent all experiments build on; F1 (support working-set) and F5 (the only gain) show which structural moves actually change this construction versus which are dead ends.

plan.analysis: Line L1 is stuck at 0.940795; every local perturbation (F9-F18, F6) returns the start unchanged, so the basin is exhausted. The gap to 1 is 5.9%, and R=1 requires f*f to be a flat rectangle. I bet on three global structural changes rather than more local polish: (1) Fourier phase retrieval that directly imposes a flat autoconvolution, (2) a low-dimensional superposition of inverse-square-root singularities, whose truncated autoconvolutions are flat plateaus, and (3) direct L2 gradient descent onto an explicit trapezoid target in the knot domain. Each is a different basin and each uses the whole 60 s.

experiments.hypothesis: R=1 is attained only when f*f is flat; local gradient methods cannot impose that global Fourier constraint. Alternating projections in Fourier between nonnegative f and a target flat autoconvolution can jump to a different basin that local polishing cannot reach.
experiments.change: Implement a Gerchberg-Saxton style construct: take start p0002, compute g=_knots(f) and M=max(g). Set support [a,b] where g>0.01*M, and build target Gt as a trapezoid of height M on [a,b] with ramp width 0.05*(b-a). Zero-pad f to length 2N. Iterate 3000 times: F=fft(f_pad); Ghat=fft(Gt_pad); Fnew=sqrt(abs(Ghat))*exp(1j*angle(F)); fnew=real(ifft(Fnew)); clip fnew to >=0; enforce support outside [a,b] to zero; rescale so sum(fnew)=sum(f). Every 100 iterations evaluate exact R on the current f and keep the best. Finally run the existing _lbfgs_log and peak polish on the best f. Use budget_seconds*0.95.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R>0.95 on L1. Result will show whether the Fourier-flat target produces a g with >60% of knots within 1% of max; if R stays <=0.940795 it shows the flat-rectangle target is unreachable from this basin by Fourier projection.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact convolution of two one-sided x^{-1/2} singularities is a flat plateau, so a small sum of truncated singularities can produce a much flatter f*f than the current spiky construction. This is a low-dimensional family that global optimisation can explore.
experiments.change: Ignore start. Build f on N=4000 steps as f_i = sum_{k=1..K} a_k / sqrt(max(eps, (i+0.5)/N - x_k)) for i/N > x_k and i/N <= L, else 0, with K=4, eps=1e-6, and parameters x_k in [0,L), a_k>0, L in (0,1]. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on parameters (x_k/L, log a_k, L) to maximise exact R, 2000 iterations, population 20. Take the best parameter set, prolongate to N=84992 by evaluating the same continuous formula on the finer grid, rescale, and run the existing _lbfgs_log plus peak-window polish until the deadline. Print the fitted parameters and final R.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R>0.95. The result will show whether a K=4 singularity superposition can beat 0.940795; if the best R is below 0.94, it indicates the singularity family is not competitive and the p0002 basin is close to the optimum for such shapes.

experiments.hypothesis: The ratio objective has a non-smooth max that stalls L-BFGS. Directly minimising ||f*f - trapezoid||^2 removes the max and explicitly fills valleys, which should flatten f*f and raise R.
experiments.change: From p0002, compute g=_knots(f), M=max(g), support [a,b] where g>0.02*M, ramp r=0.1*(b-a). Build target Gt: 0 outside [a,b], M on [a+r,b-r], linear ramps between. Define E=0.5*sum((g-Gt)^2). Implement analytic gradient: dE/dh = 2*correlate(g-Gt, h) (use fftconvolve with reversed h, mode 'valid', take first N). Minimise E over h>=0 with L-BFGS-B in log space (reuse _lbfgs_log structure but replace _fun_grad with this E and gradient). Print E, R, and the fraction of knots within 1% of max.

plan.analysis: L2: 0.940795 has survived eight distinct perturbations (coarse-to-fine in both directions, soft-max, component relocation, unbounded resolution ladder) and F6 says the point is robust to every local move tried, so only a genuinely new basin or a curvature-based escape can help. Bets: (a) random coarse multistart + ladder to reach a different basin entirely; (b) a Lanczos negative-curvature escape — the one mechanism never tried at this plateau. L3: gains from finer N are shrinking (F29 +0.0058 at 32k, F30 +0.0020 at 205k), and its basin is smooth and low-contrast (max/mean 4.6, 0% zeros) while the 0.94 regime is spiky (97:1, 21% zeros, off-centre peak). Bet: a big move — replace L3's basin with sparse high-dynamic-range multistart ladders.

experiments.hypothesis: The 0.940795 point is a local optimum reached by descent from the warm start; random coarse starts refined upward can land in a different basin whose full-resolution polish exceeds it, since every perturbation of p0028 itself is absorbed by that basin (F6, F17, F25, F26, F27).
experiments.change: Ignore p0028's shape except as a fallback. Polish each at N0 with _lbfgs_log(800 iters) and take the top 5. For each of the top 5, run a doubling ladder N0->1024->2048->...->32768->42496 using _prolongate, at each level _lbfgs_log(500 iters) followed by _window_polish_peak(frac 0.25, extra 16); after every level record R_of. Spend remaining time (up to deadline-1s) doing _lbfgs_log + peak-polish on the best ladder result, then return the better of that and the rescaled start p0028.
experiments.prediction: Aim: >0.9410 (i.e. a genuine new basin). Diagnostic: if any ladder reaches R>0.93 at 8192 steps but collapses back to 0.940795 at 42496, the basin is unique and strong; if nothing exceeds 0.90 at any level, random sparse starts cannot reach the high-contrast regime at these sizes.

experiments.hypothesis: The plateau is likely a constrained local max with many near-max knots (42.8% within 5% of max); if it is only a saddle or a flat valley, the negative-curvature direction of the reduced Hessian over the nonzero coordinates will lead to a better point, and no experiment has yet used curvature information.
experiments.change: Take p0028, active = indices with h>1e-8*max(h), define g(u) = gradient of -log R w.r.t. active heights (reuse _fun_grad, return g[active]). If lambda_min<0: for alpha in {0.5,1,2,4}*alpha0 with alpha0 = 0.01*max(h)/max|v|, set h' = clip(h+alpha*v,0), rescale, run full _lbfgs_log(1500 iters) + _window_polish_peak(0.3,16), keep if R improves; loop up to 8 escapes inside the budget. If lambda_min>=0 (positive definite), do the same along the *flattest* eigenvector and record it, then finish with a full _lbfgs_log polish and return the best of all candidates and the start.
experiments.prediction: Aim: 0.9415+. Diagnostic to report: lambda_min of the reduced Hessian at p0028 (a small negative value means the plateau is escapable by curvature; lambda_min>=0 with all escapes returning to 0.940795 proves the point is a genuine second-order local max).

plan.analysis: L2 (0.940795) has survived every local and soft-max escape tried (F31–F40): the plateau is structural at fixed knot geometry, and the 0.94 regime is spiky (97:1, 21% zeros). The untested lever is the knot geometry itself — moving/splitting the spikes of the incumbent at coarse resolution rather than reweighting fixed steps; that is what I bet on there. L3 (0.826931) is a smooth local basin that keeps paying a little for resolution (F41) and keeps rejecting from-scratch sparse starts (F32/F35/F42) because L-BFGS refills zeros. Two distinct bets: (a) forbid refilling by optimising on a *constrained* zero mask and unfreezing progressively; (b) directly flatten the top of f*f with a fixed-beta logsumexp surrogate (never tried on L3, whose peak is rounded and responsive, unlike L2's kink).

experiments.hypothesis: The 0.940795 ceiling is a limit of the incumbent's *knot positions*, not of its heights: every height-only or soft-max move returns it unchanged. Re-optimising the spike geometry (integer moves/merges of a coarse spike train) changes the combinatorial arrangement that sets the flat top of f*f, which is exactly what the ratio rewards.
experiments.change: Coarsen p0028 to Nc=2048 (mass-conserving sum of blocks) and extract its spikes as a list of (index, height) with K<=300 entries (threshold 1e-4*max, each run of nonzero steps -> one spike with its summed mass on the run's centre index). Then run coordinate descent on the *geometry* at Nc: loop over spikes in random order, for each try shifting its index by ±1,±2,±3,±5 (merge mass if it lands on an existing spike, drop if it leaves [0,Nc-1]) and accept if R at Nc increases by >1e-12; after each full sweep re-optimise the spike heights with _lbfgs_block(maxiter=300) on the nonzero indices only. Do ~60 sweeps or until 25 s used. Then take the best coarse spike train, _prolongate to 42496, _rescale, and run _lbfgs_log(800) + _window_polish_peak(frac=0.15, extra=16) + _lbfgs_log(800) alternating until the deadline. Return the better of that and the rescaled start (compare R_of). Use the full budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.9415 on L2 (clearly above the 0.940795 plateau). Diagnostic: if R at Nc=2048 of the moved spike train exceeds R of the plain coarsened p0028 by >= 2e-3 at the same Nc, geometry is the binding constraint; the returned shape should show max/mean > 120 and a larger zero fraction (>25%) than p0028's 20.9%. If no coarse geometric move is accepted at all, the plateau is structural in the spike arrangement and the returned array will be the start.

experiments.hypothesis: Sparse starts collapse back into the smooth 0.827 basin only because L-BFGS is free to refill zeros (F35, F42). If the zero set is a hard constraint during optimisation and only released progressively, the optimiser is forced to reach a high-dynamic-range shape at low N, which can then be grown.
experiments.change: Coarsen p0050 to N0=16384 (mass-conserving cumulative interpolation). Build a mask: pick contiguous blocks of width w~U{1,64} covering ~35% of the steps and set them to zero (preferentially at the lowest |h| positions, keep step 0 and N0-1 nonzero). Freeze those entries to zero and optimise only the free entries with _lbfgs_block(maxiter=400, deadline). Then run 6 unfreeze rounds: each round release one third of the still-frozen entries that are adjacent to a nonzero entry (ties by larger neighbouring mass), re-optimise the free set, and record R; total ~8 optimisations at N0 = 16384. Keep two branches alive (the best R and the spikiest by max/mean) and ladder only the better one: _prolongate to 65536, _rescale, _lbfgs_log(600) + _window_polish_peak(0.10, 8); then to 131072 and 262144 if >= 15 s remain, each with _lbfgs_log(600) + _window_polish_peak(0.05,4) + _window_polish_peak(0.10,8). Spend the remaining time alternating _lbfgs_log(800) and _window_polish_peak(0.10,8) on the best, and return the better of that and the rescaled start.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.840 on L3. Diagnostic: after the final unfreeze round at N0, zeros fraction still >= 15% and max/mean >= 8 means a genuinely different basin was reached and the ladder should carry it past 0.83; if zeros fill back in and R at N0 sits at ~0.827, the smooth basin survives even hard support constraints and the returned shape will again be max/mean ~4.5 with the peak near 0.55 of the support.

experiments.hypothesis: The L3 solution's f*f top is much narrower than L2's (19.6% of knots within 1% of max vs 33.9%), so R is still limited by peak sharpness. A logsumexp surrogate with a moderate *fixed* beta pushes all near-max knots toward equality (widening the flat top) instead of chasing the single argmax; on L3's smooth rounded peak this surrogate is well-conditioned, unlike the kinked L2 case where it failed.
experiments.change: Add _fun_grad_sm(h, beta): build Lf=_knots(h); with M=Lf.max() and w=exp(beta*(Lf-M)); S=w.sum(); Lm_s = M + log(S)/beta; num as usual; gLf = -dq/num with gLf[m] replaced by the soft weights gLf += beta*w/S (i.e. d(log Lm_s)/dLf_j = w_j/S ... implement as gLf += w/S, the derivative of log Lm_s times ... note: d Lm_s/dLf_j = w_j/S). L-BFGS in log-heights with the same jac wrapper as _lbfgs_log. Run at N=32768 (coarsened p0050): for beta in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64} (L normalised to unit max) run _lbfgs_sm up to 300 iterations, then a true-objective _lbfgs_log(400) + _window_polish_peak(0.10,8), keeping the true-objective best. If a true-objective improvement over the start appears at 32768, ladder it 65536 -> 131072 -> 262144 with a shortened homotopy (beta in {16,64}) plus true-objective polish at each level; otherwise spend the remaining budget on the true-objective polish loop (_lbfgs_log + _window_polish_peak(0.10,8) alternations) on the incumbent. Return the best, never worse than the rescaled start.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.838 on L3. Diagnostic: the share of f*f knots within 1% of the maximum should rise from 19.6% to >= 25% while max/mean stays near 4-6; if the 1%-share does not move (stays ~19.6%) the peak is already as flat as this construction allows and the surrogate is inert, which the result will show as R within 1e-6 of 0.826931.

plan.analysis: L3: p0056's +0.054 jump came from the logsumexp soft-max homotopy on a smooth base, and it left a spiky construction (max/mean 230, 16.3% zeros) frozen at N=32768 — the higher-resolution ladder in that program never produced an accepted candidate (58.6 s went to N=32768 polish). So the peak-sharpening direction is proven but unexploited at fine resolution: prolongate p0056 and re-run the homotopy at doubled N, with a low-beta re-warm because the basin is now rough. L4 is fresh at 0.667 with a constant start: two genuinely different constructions to compare — (a) smooth multiscale ladder driven by the L3-winning logsumexp surrogate, (b) sparse multiblock seeds (F35-style) which is the only route that has ever produced max/mean>100 shapes.

experiments.hypothesis: p0056's gain came from widening/reshaping the f*f top at N=32768 only; its spiky shape (16.3% zeros, max/mean 230) has structure finer than one step of 1/32768, so the same logsumexp homotopy applied after prolongation to 65536/131072 can sharpen the peak region further while the true-objective polish preserves the spiky basin.
experiments.change: Load p0056. For N in (65536, 131072, 262144): _prolongate(best, N), _rescale, then run the logsumexp homotopy _lbfgs_sm for beta in (2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) at maxiter 250 each, evaluating R_of after every beta and keeping the incumbent only on true-objective improvement; after the homotopy at each level run _lbfgs_log(600) then _window_polish_peak(frac=0.05, extra=8) and _window_polish_peak(frac=0.10, extra=16). Advance to the next N only if R_of improved by >1e-6 at the current level; otherwise keep polishing at the current N. Whatever time remains: alternate _lbfgs_log(1500) and peak-window polish (frac 0.05/0.10/0.20) until deadline-1 s, always returning the best-scoring array seen (never worse than rescaled p0056). Print R after each beta and each level.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.895 on L3. Diagnostic: the 0.1%-near-max knot share should rise above 11.83% and max/mean stay >=100; if R is flat at 0.880983 across all levels, 32768 already resolves the spike and the next move must be structural (e.g. exact-coincidence peak design) rather than resolution.

experiments.hypothesis: From a flat constant start the smooth basin is reachable and, once there, the L3-winning logsumexp soft-max surrogate can push the f*f top much harder than plain hard-max L-BFGS (F43 vs F41 on L3), giving L4 a strong first climb.
experiments.change: Start from ones(64). Ladder N = 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16000, 32000, 64000: at each level _prolongate + _rescale, then _lbfgs_log(400), then a logsumexp homotopy _lbfgs_sm for beta in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64) at maxiter 200 (accept only if R_of improves), then _window_polish_peak(frac=0.05, extra=4) and (frac=0.10, extra=8). Do not stop the ladder early — keep doubling while >6 s remain. After the ladder, spend all remaining budget alternating _lbfgs_log(1500) with peak-window polish (frac 0.05/0.10/0.20) at the largest N reached, keeping the best. Print R and N per level.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.84 (a large, immediate gain over 0.666667); diagnostic: the 1%-near-max share should exceed 20% and max/mean should grow well past 4, showing whether the smooth basin alone is competitive with the spiky regime on this fresh line.

experiments.hypothesis: The high-R regime elsewhere is spiky (max/mean 100-230, 15-20% zeros); the smooth basin is a strong local attractor, so a sparse multiblock seed ladder is the way to reach it from a blank line, and on a fresh line it is not competing against an incumbent smooth solution.
experiments.change: Build _random_sparse_start as in F35: B ~ U{8,40} blocks with log-uniform widths in [1,60] and log-uniform heights in [1,300], zeroing 40-70% of entries, at N0=1024. Run 40 such seeds with _lbfgs_log(500) (hard max, no surrogate) and keep the top 6 by R_of. Ladder all 6 through N = 4096, 16000, 32000, 64000, 128000: at each level _prolongate, _rescale, _lbfgs_log(400), _window_polish_peak(frac=0.10, extra=8); prune to the best 3 after N=16000 and to the best 1 after N=32000. Spend any remaining time on _lbfgs_log(1500) + peak-window polish of the leader. Return the best, never worse than the rescaled start. Print per-seed R and per-level best.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.86 — beat the smooth-ladder experiment in the same generation if the spiky basin dominates. Diagnostic: the winner should show max/mean > 50 and >=10% zeros; if instead the best sparse seed only reaches ~0.83, the spiky basin is not reachable from multicontact seeds on L4 and the smooth ladder is the right branch.

plan.analysis: L3 is at 0.880983, a spiky local optimum (max/mean 230, 16.3% zeros). F49/p0059 showed that prolonging this exact shape to 65536-262144 and re-running the beta homotopy is inert, so L3 needs a basin change, not more resolution: perturbed spiky restarts plus fresh sparse multiscale seeds relocked with the analytic-gradient logsumexp surrogate (the mechanism that produced the +0.054 jump in F43, and that worked once before on L3 as F35). L4 is at only 0.788774 at N=512 with a smooth shape; its code uses finite-difference gradients, so its ladder to 64000 never actually optimised at larger N. Bet one: porting p0056's exact-gradient surrogate pipeline to L4 should at least reach the smooth-basin ceiling (~0.83). Bet two: with a working surrogate, L4 can be driven into the spiky regime (max/mean >> 3) which is where 0.88 lives — F51 failed only because it used hard-max, not the surrogate.

experiments.hypothesis: 0.880983 is a single isolated spiky basin: the beta-homotopy landed there from the smooth start and F49 proved the shape cannot be refined at higher N. Other spiky basins of the same qualitative family (sparse, max/mean 100-1000) should have higher R, and they are reachable only by perturbing/seeding the shape and relocking with the same logsumexp homotopy that created it (F43, F35).
experiments.change: Keep p0056's helpers (_num_and_dq, _backprop, _fun_grad, _fun_grad_sm, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_sm, _window_polish_peak). Add a restart loop that runs until 1 s before deadline: (i) block-perturb the incumbent - cut its 32768 steps into B in {64,128,256} contiguous blocks, multiply each block by a log-uniform factor in [exp(-1),exp(1)], zero 10-30% of randomly chosen blocks; (ii) fresh sparse multiscale seed at N0=8192 - 20-40 log-uniform-width blocks with heights log-uniform in [30,1000], 40-70% of entries zeroed, rescaled. For each candidate run the beta homotopy beta = 2,4,8,16,32,64,128 (maxiter 250 each), then true-objective _lbfgs_log(600) + _window_polish_peak(frac 0.10, extra 8); accept only if R_of improves. Ladder any improved candidate to 65536 only if it beats 0.880983, and between restarts hard-threshold heights below 1e-3*max to exact zero. Return the best of all candidates and the rescaled p0056.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.89 on L3. Diagnostic: report how many perturbed/seed restarts land within 1e-4 of 0.880983 - if most do, the basin is isolated and this construction family is exhausted; a new best should come with higher max/mean than 230 and a 1%-near-max share above 24.3%.

experiments.hypothesis: p0061's ladder reached N=64000 but its objective uses scipy finite differences, so every L-BFGS step costs O(N) autoconvolutions and no real optimisation happened above N=512. Replacing it with p0056's exact analytic gradient (backprop through the autoconvolution) makes the same logsumexp homotopy that gave L3 +0.054 affordable at N=16384-65536, which should push L4 past the smooth ceiling.
experiments.change: Start from p0061's heights, prolongated by cumulative-mass interpolation to N=16384. Copy p0056's exact-gradient machinery verbatim (_knots, _num_and_dq, _backprop via fftconvolve above 1500 steps, _fun_grad, _fun_grad_sm, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_sm in log-heights with jac=True, _window_polish_peak on the argmax neighbourhood). Run _lbfgs_log(maxiter 600), then the beta homotopy beta = 4,8,16,32,64 at maxiter 300, after each beta run _lbfgs_log(400) + _window_polish_peak(frac 0.10, extra 8, then frac 0.20, extra 16), keeping the true-objective best only. If R beats 0.788774, ladder 32768 then 65536 with a shortened homotopy (16,64) and the same polish; then spend the remaining time alternating _lbfgs_log(1500) and peak-window polish (frac 0.05/0.10/0.20) until 1 s before the deadline. Never return worse than the rescaled start; print R, N, max/mean and the 1%-near-max share per level.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.84 on L4 (from 0.788774). Diagnostic: with exact gradients N should climb past 4096 while R still rises; if R stalls near 0.80-0.81 with max/mean still ~3, the smooth basin is capped and the spiky route is L4's only path.

experiments.hypothesis: L4's best (0.788774, smooth, max/mean 3.2) sits far below L3's 0.881, which is spiky (max/mean 230). F51's sparse seeds collapsed on L4 only because they were polished with the hard-max objective; with the logsumexp surrogate and exact gradients those seeds should hold their spiky structure and reach a much better basin.
experiments.change: Include p0056's exact-gradient surrogate machinery (_fun_grad, _fun_grad_sm, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_sm, _backprop, _window_polish_peak). Generate 20-30 random sparse multiscale starts at N0=4096: B ~ U{10,40} log-uniform widths in [1,60], block heights log-uniform in [30,1000], zero 40-70% of entries, rescale. For each seed run the beta homotopy (beta 2,4,8,16,32,64, maxiter 200) followed by true-objective _lbfgs_log(400); keep the top 3 by R_of. Prolongate each to 16384 then 32768, re-running homotopy (16,64) plus _lbfgs_log(400) and peak polish at each level, keeping the global best. Then, until 1 s before the deadline, block-perturb the best (multiply 64-256 contiguous blocks by log-uniform factors in [0.4,2.5], zero 10-25% of blocks) and relock with the homotopy plus true polish, accepting only improvements. Return the best candidate, never worse than the rescaled p0061; print seeds' scores and max/mean.

Form two seeds: s1 = sqrt(e * h0), s2 = (e**0.25) * (h0**0.75). For each seed run exact-gradient logsumexp homotopy with beta in (8,32,128,512), maxiter 300 each, accepting only true R improvements; then run exact _fun_grad full polish and peak-window polish at fracs (0.20,0.08,0.03). Keep the best of both seeds and p0078. With remaining time, run multiplicative log-normal perturbation restarts only on the active entries inside the central peak window, each followed by exact polish. Use the full budget and print R after each stage.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >0.88155 on L3. Success is shown by the 1%-near-max f*f share rising above ~24.5% while max/mean stays above 80; if both hybrid seeds polish back to 0.881416 within 1e-5, the envelope/spike decomposition does not escape p0078's basin.

experiments.hypothesis: p0079 stopped at N=4096 because F68's gate blocked higher levels, but its flat-top shape has only max/mean ~41 versus L3's spiky basin; a higher-beta continuation at N=8192 with active-set pruning can sharpen the top without letting newly created tiny entries destabilize the true R.
experiments.change: Load p0079, prolongate by cumulative mass to N=8192. Run active-set log-LBFGS on entries above 1e-10 of max, with logsumexp betas (32,128,512,1024,2048), maxiter 250 each, accepting only exact-R improvements. After each beta, prune entries below 1e-12 of max and re-run exact _fun_grad L-BFGS on the remaining active set. Then run peak-window exact polishes with fracs (0.30,0.15,0.07,0.03). Do not use a gate: keep the best array over N=4096 and N=8192, and continue alternating high-beta and exact polish until the deadline. Print exact R at every beta and level.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >0.8782 on L4 at N=8192. Success shows as 1%-near-max f*f share >34.5% and max/mean >45 while exact R exceeds 0.877297; if high-beta polishing drops below p0079 and never recovers, N=8192 refinement is not useful for this flat-top basin.

experiments.hypothesis: The logsumexp surrogate only softens the max; R is maximized when f*f is box-like, so directly penalizing deviations from a flat top over the near-max band should move p0079's shape more effectively than another unconstrained polish.
experiments.change: Load p0079 at N=4096. Add an auxiliary objective J = -R + lambda * mean(((g/M)-1)^2 over knots with g >= 0.90 M), where g = conv(h,h) and M=max(g). Implement its gradient by backpropagating the extra quadratic penalty through conv, with lambda annealed over (1e-1, 3e-2, 1e-2, 3e-3, 0). At each lambda run L-BFGS-B on log h for 250 iters, then at lambda=0 run exact _fun_grad polish and peak-window polishes at fracs (0.25,0.10,0.04). Accept only exact-R improvements over p0079. If R improves at N=4096, prolongate by cumulative mass to N=8192 and repeat a shortened lambda schedule (3e-2,1e-2,0) plus exact polish; otherwise spend the remaining budget on repeated lambda=0 peak-window polishes. Print R and the near-max fraction after each lambda.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >0.8780 on L4, with the diagnostic that the 1%-near-max f*f share rises above 35% while exact R improves. If the penalty raises the flat-top share but exact R falls or never exceeds p0079, flattening the near-max band is not the limiting factor for this construction.

plan.analysis: L3's gain came from F73's one-shot envelope/spike decomposition; direct polish is stuck, so the best bet is to iterate that decomposition on the new incumbent and vary the envelope width. L4 is still climbing by resolution: p0088 was F74's N=8192 step, so continue the ladder with active-set/high-beta polish. In parallel, test whether L3's spiky decomposition can escape L4's flat-top basin, which has more near-max knots but lower R. Avoid the failed flat-top penalty and one-shot reorderings.

experiments.hypothesis: F73 found a better basin by splitting p0078 into a smooth envelope and fine spikes; applying the same split repeatedly to p0087, with several envelope widths, should keep sharpening the two scales and raise R where direct polish has stalled.
experiments.change: Implement an iterative decomposition loop starting from p0087. Each round: normalize h to unit max; choose a Gaussian width cycling through N/64, N/32, N/128; build e with _gaussian_envelope and seed s=sqrt(e*h); run _lbfgs_sm with betas (8,32,128,512), maxiter 200 each, accepting only exact R gains; then run _lbfgs_log full exact polish and _window_polish_peak at fracs (0.20,0.08,0.03). If a round improves exact R, replace h and repeat with the next width. If no round improves after two tries, do multiplicative log-normal perturbations only on active entries inside the peak window followed by exact polish. Keep p0087 as fallback and run until close to the deadline.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >0.8826 on L3 (stretch 0.8830). Success shows as exact R above 0.882324; the 1%-near-max f*f share should rise above ~22.7% or max/mean above ~250. If every seed polishes back to 0.882324 within 1e-5, iterated decomposition is not escaping this basin.

experiments.hypothesis: p0088 was obtained by F74's first prolongation to N=8192; the ladder stopped there. experiments.change: Load p0088. For N in (16384, 32768): prolongate by cumulative mass; run active-set log-LBFGS on entries above 1e-10 of max using _fun_grad, then high-beta _lbfgs_sm with betas (128,512,1024,2048,4096), maxiter 200 each; after each beta prune entries below 1e-12 of max and re-run exact active-set polish; then run exact peak-window polishes at fracs (0.30,0.15,0.07,0.03). Accept only exact-R improvements and keep the best array over all N. If N=16384 scores more than 0.002 below the incumbent, skip to N=32768; otherwise spend remaining time alternating high-beta and exact/window polish at the best N. Use the full budget and print exact R at each level.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >0.8798 on L4 at N=16384 or N=32768 (stretch 0.8805). Success shows as exact R above 0.878872, with the 1%-near-max f*f share above ~34.5% and max/mean above ~60. If both higher levels polish below p0088, the flat-top basin is saturated at N=8192.

plan.analysis: L3 is stuck at p0087 (0.882324): same-resolution envelope reseeding (F79), fine-grid prolongation (F84), and reordered polish (F76) all failed, but coarse-grid search (F52/F60) and coarsen/reprolongate (F56) worked earlier on L3. Bet: escape p0087 by optimising a coarse multiscale representation, then prolongating back. L4 is stuck at p0088 (0.878872): upward prolongation (F80) and envelope reseeding (F81) failed, and the flat-top basin has only max/mean 52. Bet on two larger structural changes: random sparse multiscale starts at coarse N, and direct non-negative full-vector L-BFGS instead of the log parameterisation.

experiments.hypothesis: p0087 is trapped at N=32768 by grid-aligned spikes. A coarse multiscale representation (N=2048-4096) removes fine spike alignment, and random block perturbations at that scale can find a nearby better basin; prolongating back recovers fine detail. This is the coarse-grid mechanism that worked in F52/F60, not the same-resolution reseeding that failed in F79.
experiments.change: Load p0087. Coarsen by cumulative mass to N=2048. Build 20 random multiscale perturbations: choose 8-24 log-uniform widths, multiply the coarse active blocks by exp(normal(0,0.15)), smooth once with a 3-point kernel, then run exact log-LBFGS (_lbfgs_log, 300 iters) at N=2048, keeping only exact-R improvements. Take the best 2 coarse candidates, prolongate each by cumulative mass back to N=32768, and run: exact log-LBFGS 600 iters; peak-window polish at fracs 0.10, 0.04, 0.015 (extra=8); then a final exact polish. Accept only exact R > p0087. Use all remaining time for one more coarse restart cycle.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R > 0.88240 on L3. Success shows as the 1%-near-max f*f share rising above 23.0% while max/mean stays above 150; if every coarse candidate returns to 0.882324 within 1e-5, coarse-grid escape does not work on this spiky basin.

experiments.hypothesis: L4's N=8192 flat-top basin is a local optimum: upward prolongation (F80) and envelope reseeding (F81) failed. A random sparse multiscale search at N=1024, followed by prolongation to N=8192, can reach a different flat-top basin with more near-max knots. This is the F35/F52 coarse-global mechanism, not yet tried on L4.
experiments.change: Load p0088 only as the incumbent. Build 24 random sparse multiscale seeds at N=1024: each has 12-40 blocks with log-uniform widths, heights log-uniform in [1e-3,1], one smoothing pass; run exact log-LBFGS 300 iters at N=1024 on each. Keep the top 3 by exact R. For each, prolongate by cumulative mass to N=8192, then run: high-beta logsumexp homotopy betas 32,128,512,1024,2048 (200 iters each); active-set exact log-LBFGS on entries above 1e-10 of max; peak-window exact polish fracs 0.30,0.15,0.07,0.03. Accept only exact R > p0088 and keep the best array. Use the full budget; if no random seed beats p0088 after homotopy, spend remaining time on two more coarse seeds.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R > 0.87920 on L4. Success is a random-seed candidate exceeding p0088 before final polish, or final 1%-near-max f*f share above 34.5% with max/mean above 55; if all coarse seeds polish below 0.878872, L4's basin is not reachable from sparse coarse starts.

experiments.hypothesis: p0088 was polished only in log-height coordinates, which can freeze entries near the positivity boundary and limit reshaping of the flat top. Direct non-negative L-BFGS-B on the full height vector explores a different local geometry and was effective on L3 in F59. Applying it at N=8192 with active-set and window alternation may flatten the f*f top further.
experiments.change: Load p0088 at N=8192. Run direct full-vector L-BFGS-B with bounds (0,None), exact _fun_grad/_R_of, maxiter 800, on all entries; take the result. Prune entries below 1e-10 of max to zero, then re-run direct L-BFGS-B on the remaining positive entries (400 iters), then a peak-window direct polish at fracs 0.30,0.15,0.07,0.03. Repeat this direct-polish cycle twice with small multiplicative perturbations (sigma 0.01) on the central peak window before each direct run. Accept only exact R > p0088. Use all remaining budget on further direct-polish cycles.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R > 0.87900 on L4. Success is a measurable rise in the 1%-near-max f*f share above 33.6% while max/mean stays above 50; if direct-coordinate polish returns exactly to 0.878872, the log parameterisation is not the limiting factor for this flat-top basin.

info.open_why: Inspect the two line-best programs and the findings that produced/refined them (envelope-spike reseeding F73, prolongation+logsumexp F74, multi-beta continuation F82, perturbation restarts F65) to design non-repeating experiments for L3 and L4.

plan.analysis: L3's p0099 is a genuinely new basin (+0.080 in one step) reached by smooth-max (logsumexp) polishing that broadened the f*f top; its 0.1%-near-max share is still only 4.9%, so the peak is far from flat and there is room. Bet: keep pushing that same broadening/sharpening machinery on the new basin, at higher resolution and with a stronger (lower-beta) broadening pass, rather than reverting to perturbation tricks that were tuned for the old spiky family. L4 is stuck: three structural moves (upward prolongation F80, envelope reseeding F81, random coarse seeds F86, direct non-negative L-BFGS F87) all returned the start unchanged, and its f*f max sits at 0.78 of support. Bet: change the search space rather than the optimizer — mass-coarsen the incumbent and let low-beta smoothing restructure the peak on a coarse grid, then re-prolongate.

experiments.hypothesis: p0099 is under-resolved: N=32000 with 14.6% zeros and max/mean 58.7 leaves the fine spike pattern coarse, so the 0.1%-near-max share (4.9%) is limited by grid effects rather than by the shape. The same smooth-max ladder that produced the +0.080 jump should keep paying at doubled resolution, where the same shape has finer degrees of freedom and the exact max is resolved better.
experiments.change: Load p0099 (N=32000) as `start`; keep it as incumbent with its exact R. Cumulative-mass prolongate it to N=64000 (interp on cumsum, diff, clip>=0, rescale). At N=64000 run p0099's own ladder: for beta in (200, 600, 1500, 4000) call _lbfgs_sm(400 iters), accept only on exact R; after each beta run _lbfgs_log(800 iters) and _window_polish_peak with fracs (0.40, 0.15, 0.05) and extra 20 at beta=800 (400 iters); then loop exact _lbfgs_log + 0.05/0.03 window polishes until the deadline. Return the best array measured by exact R over all of {p0099 at 32000, anything at 64000}; print exact R after every stage. Do not stop early.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >0.9100 on L3. Success shows as the 1%-near-max f*f share rising above 28.4% and the 0.1% share above 4.9% at N=64000; if every 64000 step returns <=0.906686, resolution escalation is exhausted for this basin and the gain must come from reshaping at fixed N.

experiments.hypothesis: R rises when f*f is box-like, and p0099's top is still sharply peaked (only 4.9% of knots within 0.1% of max vs 33.7% within 5%). The +0.080 gain came from moderate betas; a deliberate down-then-up beta homotopy, starting with much smaller betas (where the logsumexp averages over a wide band of near-max knots and drives the whole top band flat), should raise R further on this same basin without needing new resolution.
experiments.change: Load p0099 at N=32000. Use the existing _lbfgs_sm/_fun_grad_sm (logsumexp over all knots) in a descending sweep: for beta in (120, 60, 30, 15) run _lbfgs_sm with maxiter 400 from the current incumbent and keep the exact-R best (do not adopt a lower exact R). Then run an ascending re-sharpening sweep beta in (60, 200, 600, 1500, 3000), each followed by _window_polish_peak(frac 0.15/0.05, extra 8-16, beta=800) and _lbfgs_log(600 iters), all accepted only on exact R. Repeat the whole down-up cycle, interleaved with an exact-_lbfgs_log polish, until the deadline; print exact R and the 1%- and 5%-near-max shares of the current best after each cycle. plan.analysis: L3: p0109 (0.907630) beat p0099 by only +0.000944, but four different moves gained on that basin (F91 coarse re-optimisation, F92 64k prolongation, F93 descending-β flattening, F94 2-6x upsample) and F96 says they are complementary levers, never stacked: p0109 only combined coarse-escape with the sm ladder. So I bet on (1) stacking all three levers at N=64000, and (2) a coarse multigrid restart at N=2000 using p0109's own spike/zero layout with the low-β flattener before laddering up — different from failed F85, which perturbed without low-β smoothing or per-level polish. L4: p0088 has absorbed four structural moves unchanged and its f*f peaks at 0.781 of support, a different family from L3's 0.44/0.54; so the whole experiment goes on one big move — a symmetrised restart at N=512 plus symmetric-subspace ladder.

experiments.hypothesis: F91, F92 and F93 each gained on the p0099/p0109 basin but were run separately; p0109 already mixes coarse-escape with the high-β sm ladder, and its f*f top is still only 28.75% within 1% and 11.8% within 0.1% of max. Stacking coarse-escape at the fine N=64000 level (so the flattened coarse shape is refined on a grid where the plateau can actually be resolved) plus the descending-β flatten-then-sharpen cycle should produce a genuinely wider, flatter plateau instead of another +0.0005.
experiments.change: Start from p0109 (N=32000). Keep exact R_of for all accept/reject. Phase 1 (first ~30% of budget): cumulative-mass prolongate to N=64000, rescale, run _lbfgs_sm with betas (200, 600, 1500) maxiter 400 each, then _lbfgs_log maxiter 800, then _window_polish_peak(frac 0.30, extra 16, beta 800) and (0.15, extra 8, beta None). Phase 2 (~30-65%): coarse-escape at the fine level — downsample the current 64k array by cumulative mass to N=16000, run sm betas (300, 1000) + exact log-LBFGS maxiter 400 there, prolongate back to 64000, then exact log-LBFGS 600 and window polish (0.30, beta 600); do this twice, second time with N_small=8000, and once more if time remains with N_small=16000 from the newer incumbent. Phase 3 (rest, up to deadline-1s): descending-then-ascending cycle — sm betas (120, 60, 30) maxiter 250 each accepting only exact-R gains, then _lbfgs_log 600 and window polishes (0.30/0.15/0.07, extras 16/8/4) with beta None, looping until the deadline and always keeping the best exact-R array; return the runner-up as alternative. Print exact R after each phase.

experiments.hypothesis: Every gain on this basin so far came from re-optimising at a coarser effective resolution (F91: N/4) — i.e. the coarse landscape still holds untried better basins. p0109 has 28.4% zeros and max/mean 106, so its coarse shape is a spiky pattern; injecting controlled multiplicative jitter into that pattern at N=2000 and solving each seed with a low-β (flat-top) ladder before prolongating up gives a real basin search at low cost. experiments.change: Start from p0109; keep it as incumbent and fallback. Cumulative-mass downsample it to N=2000. Build 8 seeds: for each, pick 6-15 disjoint blocks of random widths (each 1.5%-8% of N) and multiply those blocks by exp(N(0,0.20)); renormalise, then run _lbfgs_sm betas (30, 120, 400) maxiter 250 each followed by _lbfgs_log maxiter 400, all at N=2000 with a ~1.5 s cap per seed, scoring each by exact R_of at N=2000 (rescale first). Take the best 3 seeds; for each, run a prolongation ladder 2000 -> 4000 -> 8000 -> 16000 -> 32000 (cumulative mass), and at each level: sm betas (150, 500) maxiter 250, exact log-LBFGS maxiter 400, window polish (frac 0.25, extra 8, beta 400); accept the laddered result only if exact R at N=32000 beats the incumbent's R. Spend any remaining time alternating the best laddered array with the phase-2 coarse-escape used in experiment 1 (down to 8000 and back) and window polishes until the deadline; return the best and the second-best as alternative. Print exact R after each seed and each ladder level.
experiments.prediction: Target 0.9080+ on L3; the informative outcome is whether any coarse seed beats the incumbent's coarse R at N=2000 by >1e-4 — if yes but the ladder does not transfer, the loss is in prolongation (worth a finer ladder), while if no seed beats it the p0109 coarse basin is already the best at low N and all remaining gains are in the plateau-flattening direction.

experiments.hypothesis: p0088 (0.878872) has returned unchanged under four structural moves (F80 higher N, F81 envelope reseeding, F86 sparse seeds, F87 direct non-negative L-BFGS), and its f*f maximum sits at 0.781 of support — a strongly asymmetric family unlike L3's 0.44/0.54 basins. R is invariant under reversing f, so the symmetric ansatz f = reverse(f) costs nothing in attainable value but halves the free parameters (twice the effective resolution) and lands in a different basin; L3's two best programs being mirror images of each other supports this family.
experiments.change: Build h0 from p0088: cumulative-mass downsample to N=512, then symmetrise s = 0.5*(g + g[::-1]) and rescale (print R). Run a symmetric-subspace ladder, with the free vector restricted to indices 0..255 and the upper half always set to the mirrored lower half: at each N in 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, prolongate by cumulative mass (keeping symmetry by re-symmetrising after prolongation), then run _lbfgs_sm betas (16, 64, 256, 1024) maxiter 300 each on the half-vector only, then exact log-LBFGS on the half-vector maxiter 500, then a symmetric window polish that optimises only the corresponding half-window (mirror the result). Accept only on exact improvements of the full symmetrised array. In the last ~20% of budget, release the symmetry constraint: run full-vector exact log-LBFGS maxiter 600 plus window polishes (fracs 0.30/0.15/0.07) until the deadline, and return whichever of the symmetric and released arrays has higher exact R as best, the other as alternative. Print exact R after every level and after release.
experiments.prediction: Target 0.895-0.905 on L4 if the symmetric family is the right one (versus 0.878872); the diagnostic is R after the symmetric phase at N=512-2048 — a jump above 0.89 there confirms the family, while staying below 0.88 after release tells us the p0088 shape is a genuine but low-value asymetric optimum and next time the line should be restarted from a spiky coarse seed.

plan.analysis: L3 gained last gen (+0.000132) only from F115's mid-scale block perturbation of the left half, which moved the f*f peak 0.792 -> 0.539; F103 did the same on the right half earlier. So the productive lever on L3 is full-resolution 4-8 block perturbations of a half-support window plus the sm/log polish chain; I bet on (A) widening that move to a randomly placed half-support window with greedy acceptance, and (B) the same perturbation but carried up to N=64000, which no L3 experiment has combined with a perturbation. L5 is nearly saturated: p0129 gained only via the increasing-beta sm sweep (F113); perturbing windows (F117) and sm on peak windows (F120) failed, and partial zero revival (F107) failed. p0122's big L3 gain came from reviving all zeros, so I bet on global zero revival plus the sm sweep on p0129.

experiments.hypothesis: p0140 was found by perturbing only [0, 0.50N); the new f*f max sits at 0.539, so the binding structure has shifted and a half-support window placed elsewhere (randomly in [0, 0.35N]) will expose fresh degrees of freedom that the current frozen regions block.

info.open_why: Inspect the two active lines' current best programs and the findings most directly about their recent gains (smooth-max on L5, right/left-half block perturbation on L3) to design experiments that build on what actually worked on each construction.

plan.analysis: L3 is micro-plateaued: g170/g171 gains were +1.3e-4 and +4.7e-5, all from half-support block perturbations at fixed N=32000; peak-polish, sinusoidal modulation, coarse reshapes and (on p0122/p0140) prolongation all failed. But F126 shows a real win (+0.0031) from resolution growth when the prolongated level is polished hard in exact log space, not just with a softmax ladder. So L3's next step should be bigger: move p0151 up to 64000/128000 and spend the budget on exact sharp L-BFGS plus window polish there. L6 is at the trivial constant (0.6667); two independent constructions are worth having: the proven doubling ladder (F5/F50/F66) as a safe climber, and a direct spiky multiscale start (F35/F103 style) to reach a different, likely higher, basin sooner.

experiments.hypothesis: p0151's fine structure is limited by its N=32000 grid: prolongation failed earlier (F109/F122) only where it was followed by a softmax beta ladder and short polishes, whereas F126 gained +0.0031 by polishing hard in exact log space at the doubled level. Giving the doubled grid a long exact L-BFGS plus several peak-window polishes should let the near-max plateau broaden at finer scale.
experiments.change: From p0151 (N=32000): write _prolongate(h, M) = cumulative-mass resample (each new height = mass of the old interval it covers, times M/N_old), then (1) prolongate to N=64000 and run _lbfgs_log(maxiter=1200), then _lbfgs_sm with betas 400, 1500, 4000 (maxiter 300 each), then _lbfgs_log(maxiter=800), then _window_polish_peak with fracs 0.05, 0.10, 0.20 and extra 8 (maxiter 400) after each; accept the level only if exact R_of beats R_of(p0151). If accepted, prolongate that result to N=128000 and repeat the same chain with 600-iter polishes, stopping on the deadline. If 64000 is not accepted, run 6 seeded sliding-window block perturbations (window lo ~ U[0,0.35N], width 0.5N, 4-8 blocks of width 0.02-0.10*W, factor exp(N(0,0.30)), zeros revived to 1e-3 local positive mean) at N=64000 with the same exact-polish chain. Keep p0151 as fallback and always return the best exact-R construction; use the whole 60 s.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R >= 0.9097 on L3 (vs 0.908739). Success shows N=64000 (or 128000) accepted with the 0.1%-near-max f*f share above 23% and the argmax moving off 0.539; if every prolongated level is rejected by exact R, the p0151 basin is grid-saturated and only a new basin (not finer grid) can help.

experiments.hypothesis: From the constant start, the proven route is a smooth doubling ladder: prolongate by cumulative mass, soften the f*f max with logsumexp at low beta, sharpen with rising beta, then finish in exact log space. Each level starts from the previous one's polished shape, so the 60 s is spent mostly at the resolutions that matter.
experiments.change: Ignore the start's N=50. Set h = np.ones(64). For N in (64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384): h = _prolongate(h, N) (cumulative-mass resample); then for beta in (2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256): h = _lbfgs_sm(h, beta, maxiter=300, deadline) keeping the result only if R_of improves; then h = _lbfgs_log(h, maxiter=800); then h = _window_polish_peak(h, frac=0.25, extra=8, maxiter=400) and again with frac=0.10. After the ladder, while time remains, alternate _lbfgs_log(maxiter=600) with peak-window polishes at fracs 0.05/0.15/0.30 and accept only exact-R gains. If the ladder ever drops R by more than 0.01 at a level, re-polish that level once more before continuing. Return the best construction by exact R_of.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R >= 0.87 at N=16384 (clear gain over 0.666667, close to the 0.88 the same ladder reached on other lines). experiments.hypothesis: The best known constructions on this problem are spiky with ~15-25% exact zeros and a broad f*f top (L5 reached 0.9406 that way), whereas the doubling ladder lands in a smooth all-positive basin. experiments.change: From p0222: cumulative-mass prolongation to N=64000 (preserve exact zeros); hard-zero the smallest 35% of heights with no revival; renormalise positive mass; run log-space L-BFGS-B on the active support for 800 iters; then beta ladder 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 with 250 iters each, interleaved with narrow peak-window polishes (frac 0.02/0.05/0.10) at the fine grid; alternate full sharp and peak polish until the deadline.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >=0.8940 on L6 (+0.001). Success will show N=64000 with ~40% zeros and max/mean well above 40, plus a higher 0.1%-near-max share; if it stays near 0.8930, L6's smooth basin is resolution-saturated.

experiments.hypothesis: The last L7 gains came separately from stochastic peak-window perturbation and from 2x grid subdivision. Combining them should let the perturbed peak land on a finer grid and escape the 42496-step quantisation that pure polishing cannot.
experiments.change: From p0218: mass-preserving cumulative prolongation 2x to N=84992, keeping exact zeros as zeros and reviving none. Run sharp log-space L-BFGS-B 600 iters, beta sweep 1e3/1e4/1e5 (200 iters each), then 12 seeded peak-window multiplicative perturbations: window = all knots within 1% of max plus 10% pad, noise sigma 0.02-0.08, each followed by peak-window L-BFGS. Keep the best; alternate sharp full polish, beta polish, and a fresh perturbed peak polish until the deadline.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >=0.94125 on L7 (+0.00008). Success shows the finer-grid perturbed runs beat 0.941172; if all return to ~0.94117, the plateau is stable under combined subdivision and local noise.

experiments.hypothesis: p0218 has 47% exact zeros, and single-side tail revival helped on earlier L7 basins. Reviving only far-left and far-right tails, away from the f*f peak, may add low-amplitude mass that reduces the peak-to-total ratio without perturbing the main peak plateau.
experiments.change: From p0218: revive exact zeros only in the far tails [0, 0.12N) and [0.88N, N) to 1e-3 of the 256-step local mean of positive heights; leave all zeros in the central 76% exactly zero. Then run log-space L-BFGS-B 600 iters on active entries, beta ladder 1e3/1e4/1e5 interleaved with peak-window polishes frac 0.05/0.10/0.20, and alternate full sharp/peak polish to the deadline. Return the best-scoring construction, preserving p0218 if tail revival does not improve.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >=0.94122 on L7 (+0.00005). The result will show whether far-tail mass lowers ||f*f||_inf relative to the L2 numerator; a drop or unchanged score says the plateau is set by the central support, not missing tails.

info.open_why: See the exact code/plans of the current best bases on L6 and L7 and the findings that produced the recent small gains, so I can pick experiments that differ meaningfully from the just-failed granularity/sparsity moves.

plan.analysis: L7 is a near-saturated basin: gains are now ~5e-5/gen and the last real jump came from a structural move (far-tail zero revival, F183, +5.8e-5), not polishing. The remaining lever is the 6.3% exact zeros still frozen in the central 76%; I bet reviving them at a stronger level adds mass that lowers ||f*f||_inf relative to the numerator. L8 (0.8824) is a different, spiky, weak basin: its f*f near-max share is only ~22% vs L7's ~43%. L6 evidence (F128/F133/F152) shows the trivial-start doubling ladder with logsumexp softmax reaches 0.893+, well above 0.8824, so one experiment is a full fresh-start rebuild; the other applies the proven zero-revival lever (F123, +0.011 on L5) to p0105, which has 22.8% zeros and has never had revival tried.

experiments.hypothesis: F183's far-tail revival (+5.8e-5) worked by adding low-amplitude mass far from the f*f plateau. p0229 still has 6.3% exact zeros, all in the central 76%, i.e. untested degrees of freedom right where f*f is built. Reviving them at a stronger level (F183 used 1e-3; try up to 3e-2) may further lower ||f*f||_inf relative to ||f*f||_2^2.
experiments.change: From p0229: build a ladder of revival levels L in {1e-3, 5e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2}: for each, set every exact-zero entry to L times the 256-step local mean of positive heights in its neighbourhood (fallback to global positive mean where the window is all zero), rescale, run sharp log-space L-BFGS-B (600 iters on active entries), then the beta ladder 1e3/1e4/1e5 (250 iters each) each interleaved with peak-window polishes (fracs 0.05/0.10/0.20, maxiter 200); keep the first revived candidate that beats p0229's R and thereafter run the Stage-C alternation (full sharp + peak polish, 300/200 iters) on the best until ~2 s before the deadline. Return p0229 unchanged if nothing beats it.
experiments.prediction: Aim for >=0.94125 on L7 (+0.00003 or more). The printout of R per revival level shows whether central zeros are a binding constraint (higher levels gain, and zero fraction drops toward 0) or the plateau is already saturated (all levels equal, R flat at 0.94123).

experiments.hypothesis: p0105 (0.882377) has an unusually sharp f*f peak (only 21.8% of knots within 1% of max) versus the 0.89+ constructions found on L6, which have broad plateaus. p0105 likely sits in a poor local basin; the trivial-start cumulative-mass doubling ladder with logsumexp softmax (F128/F133) reached 0.893 there, far above L8's best, so rebuilding from scratch should jump the line.
experiments.change: Ignore the start's shape for the search (keep it as fallback). Build h0 = a smooth 64-step bump (e.g. 0.5+0.5cos) and run: at each level N = 64,128,...,65536, mass-preserving cumulative-mass prolongation to the next N, then log-space L-BFGS-B (400 iters) on active entries with the exact-max gradient, followed by a logsumexp softmax polish at betas 8/32/128/512/2048 (200 iters each) accepting only improvements. At N=65536 run peak-window polish (fracs 0.30/0.15/0.07/0.03, maxiter 400) and then alternate exact full L-BFGS (300 iters) with peak polish until 1.5 s before the deadline. Return the fresh candidate if its R exceeds p0105's R, else return p0105.
experiments.prediction: Target >=0.889 on L8 (+0.007). If it lands near 0.893 the line was in a bad basin and the fresh ladder is the template; if it stalls below 0.882 the L8 basin is genuinely better than the ladder at this N and the result says so via the per-level R printout.

plan.analysis: L8: F187 showed the fresh smooth-bump ladder jumps far past the old basin (0.8824 -> 0.9104) and the result is now a very spiky, zero-rich construction (60% zeros, max/mean 285, only 2% of knots within 0.1% of the f*f max). On every other line the next lever after a ladder stalls is resolution growth with cumulative-mass prolongation plus re-polish (F158, F126, F127, F143): cheap, supported, and the 0.1%-near-max share says the peak is under-resolved. Bet: prolongate p0233 2x to 131072 preserving zeros, then exact+adaptive-beta softmax+peak polish. L9 is at the trivial 0.6667; both experiments should be the proven full ladder — one from the smooth bump (F128/F133/F187, the recipe that reached 0.89-0.91 on every line), one from random sparse multiscale seeds (F35), to learn whether L9's best basin is smooth-ladder or blocky/zero-rich.

experiments.hypothesis: p0233's f*f maximum is resolved by only 2.04% of knots within 0.1% (and 5.04% within 1%), i.e. a near-triangular peak whose top is limited by the 65536 grid. On L3/L7 (F158, F126, F127, F143) doubling N by cumulative-mass prolongation followed by exact + softmax + narrow peak-window polish was the reliable next lever after a ladder stalled. p0233 is at 65536 with ~60% exact zeros; 2x cumulative-mass prolongation maps each zero step to two zero steps, so the sparse support is preserved exactly.
experiments.change: Start from p0233 (keep as fallback; return it if nothing beats it). Prolongate to N=131072 by 2x cumulative-mass interpolation (np.interp of cumsum on linspace(n+1)/linspace(m+1), diff, clip>=0) so exact zeros stay exact. Then loop until 1.5 s before the deadline: (a) exact log-space L-BFGS-B on active entries, maxiter 400; (b) softmax (logsumexp) polish with betas chosen adaptively from the knot spread near the max — compute d = M - L at the 1%/5%/20% quantiles of knots and take betas ~ {2/d1, 1/d5, 1/d20, 200, 2000} (cap at 1e6), maxiter 200 each; (c) peak-window block polish with fracs (0.10, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01), maxiter 400, windows centred on the 0.999-max region; accept a candidate only when R_of increases; after each cycle print R and the near-max share. If time remains after the 131072 loop converges, do one more 2x prolongation to 262144 and repeat (a)-(c). Use fftconvolve backprop throughout.
experiments.prediction: Target >=0.913 on L8 (+0.003 over 0.910395), with the per-cycle printout showing monotone gain at N=131072 and the 0.1%-near-max share rising above 2.04%. If the first 131072 polish cycle gives <+0.0005, the 65536 grid was not the binding constraint for this shape and the f*f-peak-share diagnostic will show it.

experiments.hypothesis: L9's only construction is the constant (0.666667). The single most reproducible move in this whole search is the cumulative-mass doubling ladder from a smooth 64-step bump with exact log-space L-BFGS plus logsumexp softmax and peak-window polish: it took L6 from 0.6667 to 0.893 (F128) and L8 from 0.8824 to 0.9104 (F187). L9 has never tried it; on a fresh line it should land in the 0.89-0.91 band.
experiments.change: Ignore the start's shape for the search (keep p0001 as fallback). h0 = (0.5+0.5*cos(2*pi*(x-0.5))) at N0=64, clipped >=1e-3, rescaled so max of f*f is 1. Loop N = 64,128,...,65536: at each level run log-space L-BFGS-B on active entries (maxiter 400, bounds -30..30), then logsumexp softmax polish at betas 8/32/128/512/2048 (200 iters each), accepting only improvements; then prolongate by cumulative-mass interpolation to the next N. At N=65536 run peak-window polish (fracs 0.30/0.15/0.07/0.03, maxiter 400), then alternate exact full L-BFGS (300 iters) with peak polish until 1.5 s before the deadline; print R at every level and cycle. Return the best of {fresh, p0001}.
experiments.prediction: Target 0.89-0.91 on L9. The per-level printout will show where the ladder saturates; if the final R is >=0.90 the L9 basin matches L8 and the next generation should copy L8's resolution-growth move, while a stall below 0.88 says the bump seed is not the right basin for this line.

experiments.hypothesis: The smooth-bump ladder converges to a specific (spiky, zero-rich) basin; F35 on L3 showed random sparse multiscale seeds sometimes reach a different, better basin (best +0.0635 over the polished incumbent). Running many cheap blocky seeds at moderate N and prolongating the winner gives L9 an independent shot at a zero-rich construction that a smooth bump may never reach, and tests whether the ladder basin is the line's best.
experiments.change: Keep p0001 as fallback. Seed stage at N0=2048: generate 24 random seeds; each has 8-40 contiguous blocks of log-uniform width (total mass normalised to 1), block heights exp(N(0,2.5)) rescaled to max 1; in half the seeds set the smallest 30-60% of blocks to exact 0 before rescaling (zero-rich variants). Polish each seed with log-space L-BFGS-B (maxiter 150) then softmax at betas 8/64/512 (100 iters each), all at N0=2048, tracking R_of. Keep the best 3 distinct seeds. Prolongate the overall best by cumulative-mass interpolation to 8192, run log-L-BFGS 400 iters + softmax 8/128/1024 + peak polish; then to 32768 and run the full final pipeline (log-L-BFGS, betas 128/1000/8000, peak-window polish fracs 0.30/0.15/0.07/0.03) alternating to 1.5 s before the deadline. Print the best seed R at N0 and the final R and zero fraction.
experiments.prediction: Target >=0.89 on L9; the diagnostic is whether any seed's N0=2048 R exceeds the smooth-bump ladder's N=2048 R from the first experiment — if so, blocky seeds find a better basin and the line should continue from the prolongated blocky incumbent, with the final zero fraction showing whether L9 prefers the 60%-zero regime seen on L8.

info.open_why: p0233 is L8's best (0.9104) and I need its full code/plan to design a stronger variant; F187 is the finding that produced it; F173/F113/F123/F158 are the strongest polish/zero-revival levers to port onto L8 and to seed L9's fresh-start ladder.

plan.analysis: L8 (0.910790) is a very spiky, 60%-zero basin with only 3.57% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max; upward prolongation to 131072 failed (F193) and fixed-N refine loops failed (F195), while seeded softmax-homotopy polishing gained (F194). The one lever never tried on L8 is F118's coarsen-then-prolongate: block-summing 4 steps leaves f exactly unchanged but frees the 65536 grid lock, so the peak region can be re-shaped in a smaller parameter space and then re-detailed. L9 (0.666667) has never had a single program survive: p0237 died on a shape bug (101 vs 100) and p0241 blew the CPU limit with 24 seeds at N0=2048. L9's binding constraint is a bug-free, time-guarded ladder that returns a plain ndarray; I bet two cheap, independent small-N ladders can both pass 0.85 and one can reach ~0.89.

experiments.hypothesis: p0236 is grid-locked at N=65536: the re-shaping of the near-triangular f*f peak (3.57% of knots within 0.1% of max) is limited by the fixed block boundaries. Block-summing 4 adjacent heights gives the identical step function (R unchanged) but a 16384-dimensional problem where the peak-feeding region can move freely; optimising there and then re-detailing should escape the lock and lift R.
experiments.change: Work from p0236 (keep it as fallback, return whichever array scores higher as a plain ndarray). Step 1: coarsen exactly by block-summing, hc = h.reshape(N//4,4).sum(axis=1) (N=65536 -> 16384); assert R_of(hc) equals the start's R to 1e-12. Step 2 (about 40% of budget): on hc run the existing pipeline hard - sharp log-space L-BFGS (600 iters), softmax logsumexp homotopy at betas 64/256/1024/4096 (250 iters each), then peak-window polish with fracs 0.30/0.15/0.07/0.03/0.015; accept only strict R gains. Step 3: prolong back to N=65536 by np.repeat(hc,4)/4 (same f, finer grid), then spend the remaining time alternating sharp log L-BFGS, softmax homotopy (betas 400..8000) and narrow peak-window polish, keeping the best array by R. Hard-guard all loops with time.process_time() and return best-so-far at 1.5 s before the deadline; print R after coarsen, after coarse optimise, and after re-detail.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.9113 (+0.0005 on L8). If the coarse stage alone already improves the function's R, the grid lock was real and the re-detail should push further; the printed 0.1%-near-max share and zero fraction show whether the peak is being flattened (share > 3.57%) or the basin simply saturates.

experiments.hypothesis: L9 has never produced a runnable program; the two failures were a shape bug and a CPU overrun, not evidence against the ladder. A minimal, defensive smooth-bump doubling ladder that returns a plain ndarray of correct shape, with explicit time gates at every stage and a fallback to best-so-far, should clear the whole 0.66 -> 0.89 range that identical ladders reached on L6.
experiments.change: Ignore the start's shape entirely (only keep it as a fallback if every stage fails; never let shapes mix - any prolongation must return exactly the requested length m, and assert h.size == m after it). Build h0 = clip(0.5+0.5*cos(2*pi*(x-0.5)), 1e-3, None) at N0=64 and rescale so max of the knot array is 1. Ladder N = 64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192: at each level run analytic-gradient log-space L-BFGS-B (400 iters max, active entries only) then a short logsumexp softmax polish at betas 8/32/128 (150 iters each), accepting only strict R gains; then cumulative-mass prolongation (cumsum on linspace(n+1), interp onto linspace(m+1), diff, clip>=0) to the next N. Between levels check time.process_time() and break with the current best if fewer than 8 s remain; hard-stop the whole ladder at 45 s, spend up to 12 s on peak-window polish of the best at its own N, then return np.asarray(best) directly. Wrap the whole body in try/except returning best-so-far. Print R at each level.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.85 on L9, ideally 0.89 (matching F128/F133's ladder on L6). The per-level printout shows where the ladder first stalls - if it plateaus by N=1024 the coarse basin is the limit, if it is still rising at 8192 then the next generation should push the grid higher.

experiments.hypothesis: A second, structurally different cheap route: F35/F146/F152 showed that sparse multiscale seeds and hard-zeroing reach different basins than a cosine bump.
