info.open_why: Inspect L8's best program and its resolution-ladder finding, plus L9's best program and the asymmetric-tilt finding that produced it, to plan one strong L8 experiment and two L9 experiments.

plan.analysis: L8 is exhausted in its own basin: last six gains total ~1e-5, and coarsening (F213), exact 2x split (F211), tilt (F212) and softmax-max (F216) all failed there. Its shape is 60% zeros, max/mean 480 — the sparse spiky regime, as L7 (0.941) also was. So L8 gets one big move: a fresh zero-rich multiscale rebuild at moderate N with a doubling ladder; keep p0266 as fallback. L9 is the opposite: smooth, no exact zeros, max/mean 3.4, deep continuation flat (F221) and sparse small-N seeds flat (F215). Two bets: (1) abandon the basin with a from-scratch smooth doubling ladder (F128/F50 route never run on L9); (2) L9 has never been optimised in a space where exact zeros can survive — every code floors at 1e-6 — so use bound-constrained L-BFGS with real pruning.

experiments.hypothesis: L8's increments are ~1e-5 because it sits in a local basin; the high-R regime across the search is sparse and spiky (L7 0.941 at 47% zeros). A fresh zero-rich multiscale search over many seeds at moderate N, then laddered up, may land in a better basin than the one inherited from p0105.
experiments.change: Keep p0266 as fallback. Build 30 deterministic random seeds at N=4096: 16-32 contiguous blocks with log-uniform widths spanning [1, N/8] and heights exp(N(0,1.5)); zero the lowest 45% of heights for half the seeds and 60% for the other half, floor the rest at 1e-3 of the max, normalise mass. For each seed run exact non-log-space L-BFGS-B on h with bounds (0, None), 200 iters (fftconvolve backprop), then 2 rounds of peak-window polish; print each seed's R. Take the top 4 seeds and, for each, run cumulative-mass prolongation 4096->16384->65536->262144 with at each rung 300-iter log-space L-BFGS plus peak polish, keeping the best-of across rungs. Return the better of that and p0266. Keep total within budget minus 2 s.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.9120 on L8. Diagnostic: a seed with ~50% exact zeros and max/mean >400 that exceeds 0.9115 would show the sparse basin is reachable and worth further seeding; if all seeds top out below 0.9100 the p0105 basin is confirmed as the only good one for this line and further gains must come from micro-polish.

experiments.hypothesis: L9's 0.7355 is the attractor of smooth local optimisation from a smooth start; the from-scratch doubling ladder that produced 0.88-0.89 on L3/L6 (F128/F50/F66) has never been run on L9, and starting at N=128 with softmax homotopy at every rung explores a different set of basins than prolonging p0255.
experiments.change: Keep p0255 as fallback. Fresh start at N=128 from three seeds: cosine^2, an off-centre Gaussian at 0.35 (width 0.2), and a two-bump sum (0.25/0.15 and 0.70/0.30). For each: at N=128 run 400-iter exact log-space L-BFGS-B, then softmax homotopy betas (8, 32, 128); then double N by cumulative-mass prolongation through 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, at each rung 400-iter log-space L-BFGS-B plus softmax homotopy betas (32,128,512,2048), stopping each rung on the time share. After the ladder, run the existing _peak_window_polish loop to convergence and print R at every rung for all three seeds. Return the best against p0255.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.80 on L9 (a break of the 0.7355 plateau would be the first real signal). Diagnostic: if all three seeds converge to ~0.73-0.74 with max/mean ~3, the plateau is a genuine attractor of smooth optimisation and L9 can only gain from a zero-rich construction; if one rung overshoots 0.78, keep laddering that seed.

experiments.hypothesis: Every L9 optimiser converts heights to log-space with a 1e-6 floor, so exact zeros can never survive (p0255 has 0% zeros, max/mean 3.38) even though the best basins elsewhere need ~50% zeros. Optimising directly in height space with non-negative bounds, and forcing pruning to exact zero between rounds, gives L9 access to that regime for the first time.
experiments.change: From p0255 (N=16384), loop until budget-3 s: (i) pick prune fraction f from a cycling schedule 0.30, 0.45, 0.60, 0.75; (ii) set the f-fraction of smallest heights to exactly 0 and clamp the rest above 1e-4 of the max; (iii) optimise h with L-BFGS-B in height space, bounds (0, None) on all entries, analytic gradient from _R_grad, 400 iters, so pruned entries may stay at 0; (iv) prolong by cumulative mass to at most 65536, re-run step (iii) at the finer grid with the same f; (v) run the peak-window polish; accept only if R beats the incumbent; print R, zero fraction and max/mean after each accepted round; keep p0255 as fallback and return the best.
experiments.prediction: Target >= 0.75 on L9 with a nonzero exact-zero fraction and max/mean >4. Diagnostic: if pruning plus height-space optimisation still returns to 0% zeros at 0.7355, zeros are genuinely useless in this basin; if R rises with f, the schedule should be pushed to larger f in later rounds.

info.open_why: L9 has 2 experiments and its last two full-budget continuations both returned the start unchanged; I need to see p0255's actual construction and why F214's tilt worked while F220/F221 failed, to pick a genuinely different direction.

plan.analysis: L8 (0.911538) is grid/basin-limited: three straight failures of local refinement and one of fresh random seeds, and its f*f top is spurious-sharp (5.0% of knots within 1% of max) while R=1 is attained only when f*f is a rectangle. Since every method so far maximised R directly (gradient dominated by the apex kink), I bet on replacing the objective with an explicit rectangle-matching loss plus exact-R polish. L9 (0.756045) is still climbing: F222's height-space + forced-pruning broke the smooth plateau, but the result still has max/mean 3.61, far from the 10-500 spiky regime of every 0.88+ basin. I bet on (a) structured spike injection — mass the pruning loop can never create — and (b) vectorising the gradient (fftconvolve + slice dinf) so the proven F222 loop can continue up the N ladder past 65536, which its np.convolve version cannot afford.

experiments.hypothesis: The optimum of R is an f*f that is a rectangle (R=1 exactly for that shape); L8's incumbent has a sharp apex with only 5% of knots within 1% of the max, so all R-gradient methods waste their signal on the peak kink. Optimising an explicit weighted rectangle-matching loss on L (flat plateau, steep shoulders, zero outside) reshapes the whole profile and can climb off this spur.
experiments.change: Keep p0266 as fallback. Work at N=65536: reduce p0266 to 65536 by cumulative-mass re-grid, restore R with the existing exact log L-BFGS + peak polish (must be >= 0.9115 or abort to fallback). Then loop until budget-4s: (1) from current L=h*h convert to knot array Lp; fit window [a,b] = knots with Lp >= 0.6*max, plateau height P = mean of Lp over the middle half of [a,b]; (2) build target T with T=P on [a,b], 0 elsewhere, and weights W = 1.0 on the inner plateau, 4.0 on the 2% transition bands at a and b (to force steep sides), 0.5 outside; (3) minimise loss = sum_j W_j (Lp_j - T_j)^2 in log-height space with analytic backprop gradient 2*backprop(W*(Lp-T)), 300 L-BFGS-B iters; (4) measure R, then run exact log L-BFGS (300 iters) + peak-window polish (fracs 0.3/0.15/0.07/0.03), keep best-of; (5) perturb the target: multiply/divide P by 1.03, shrink/expand [a,b] by 5% and 10% around its centre, cycling; (6) finally prolong the best to 262144 and 1e6 and polish briefly with the existing tools. Return best-of(start, reshaped); print R, %knots within 1% of max and ||f*f||_inf each round.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.9145 on L8. Success shows as the within-1%-of-max knot share rising from 5.0% to >= 9% (plateau flattening) with only a small drop in ||f*f||_inf (5.9676 -> ~5.90) and R still above 0.9115 after exact polish; if every targeted solve polishes back to <= 0.9116 with the same apex statistics, the L8 basin is confirmed as a strong local max and needs a different shape family, not better local search.

experiments.hypothesis: L9's basin is smooth and symmetric (max/mean 3.61, f*f max at 0.498) whereas every 0.88+ construction in this search is spiky (max/mean 10-500, 47-60% zeros). F222's pruning loop can only delete mass, never create a tall narrow spike, so the spiky regime is unreachable from it. Structured spike injection plus re-optimisation should reach it.
experiments.change: From p0271 as fallback. Loop until budget-4s: (a) pick a candidate spike deterministically cycling over positions at fractions {0.0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.90, 0.95, 0.98} of the N=16384 grid, widths {1,2,4,8,16} steps and amplitudes {2,5,15,40,100} x current max; set h[pos:pos+w] = amplitude (additive to the existing heights); (b) apply the F222 prune at f in {0.30,0.45,0.60,0.75}; (c) run height-space L-BFGS-B (bounds (0,None), analytic gradient via the existing _R_grad) 400 iters; (d) if it improves, prolong by cumulative mass to 65536, re-prune with the same f, re-run height-space L-BFGS-B 400 iters, then peak-window polish; (e) keep best-of-all and print R, zero fraction, max/mean; only adopt a candidate as the new incumbent if R strictly improves, otherwise continue the sweep. Because most attempts will lose, keep each attempt cheap by limiting the sweep to 2 L-BFGS calls before promising candidates get the full prolongation.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.78 on L9, with max/mean climbing above 8 and the f*f max moving off 0.498. Diagnostic: if every spike injection collapses back to max/mean ~3.6 and R 0.756 after polish, the smooth basin is a stable attractor and L9 needs a from-scratch spiky construction rather than perturbation.

experiments.hypothesis: L9's +0.0205 came from a mechanism (height-space bounded L-BFGS + forced pruning) that was only ever run at N<=65536, and its gradient is computed with np.convolve, which makes N>65536 unaffordable; the ceiling may therefore be grid-limited rather than basin-limited, as it was on L8 where every N increase helped.
experiments.change: Rewrite the gradient for speed without changing the maths: L = fftconvolve(h,h) (or np.convolve when n<=4000) and replace the Python loop computing dinf by a vectorised slice: dinf[max(0,m-n):min(n,m)] = 2*h[m-1-max(0,m-n) : m-min(n,m) : -1] (reversed slice of h around the peak index m).
